jobs.description:
Job Title: Design & Development Director (15-Month FTC)

Location: Norfolk / Hybrid

Reporting To: Chief Product Officer

Who We Are

At Monica Vinader, we believe luxury should be empowering, long-lasting and responsibly made. Guided by integrity, craftsmanship and innovation, our goal is to elevate people’s lives by opening access to a more beautiful world.

From crafting consciously with recycled precious metals and ethically sourced materials, to designing enduring, versatile pieces made to be layered, loved and lived in every day, we are redefining what modern jewellery can be. We create jewellery that marks moments, tells stories and becomes part of who you are, all while making responsible luxury more accessible.

Our Commitment To Sustainability, Innovation And Positive Impact Continues To Be Recognised Across The Industry. We Are Proud To Have Received

Responsible Jewellery Brand, 2026 – Country & Town House
Responsible Luxury Business of the Year, 2025 & 2026 – Positive Luxury
Top 50 Inspiring Workplaces (UK & NI), 2024 – Inspiring Workplaces

With a global footprint across physical retail, e-commerce and trusted partners, we put our community at the heart of everything we do. Proudly female-founded and inclusive, we build meaningful relationships with the people who wear and love our jewellery.

Where we need your help

The Design & Development Director leads Monica Vinader's Design & Development function and drives our creative pipeline from brief through to development sign off — the guardian of the brief, the driver of the calendar, and the person who ensures creative delivery meets our standards and pace.

We need someone with a genuinely strong point of view: someone who will sit in a critique and say clearly whether the work answers the brief, is new enough, and will sell — and hold that line with the design team, the founder and the ELT.

This is a 15 month fixed term contract with a defined mandate: land creative direction and product pipeline for FY27 and FY28 against agreed go-to-market and critical path milestones, leading a team of three direct reports covering design and product development. You will report to the Chief Product Officer.

Your time spans briefing, critique, creative planning, critical path oversight, team leadership and cross-functional work with Merchandising, Supply, Brand & Regions — a role that is detailed as well as strategic; you'll be as comfortable in a technical pack as in a boardroom.

This role requires 2-3 days per week at our Holkham (Norfolk) office, with hybrid working for the remainder, or the London office where that suits.

What You’ll Do

Role Purpose

The Design & Development Director is accountable for the brief, the plan, the commerciality and the on time delivery of Monica Vinader's design and development output. You write and own the brief, working tightly with the category team, you own the creative calendar, you chair critique, you judge the work against the brief, you drive decisions to a conclusion, and you hold the Design & Development team to the go to market and critical path calendar.

You are the single point of accountability for whether the brief is met, whether the work is developable, and when it lands. Operating in a fast paced, agile environment, you will balance granular detail with strategic thinking to drive a consistent, innovative product pipeline.

Guardian of the Brief (Accountable)

Co-create the brief: With our Head of Category Management, write and own the design brief for every project and season, so there is a single, unambiguous statement of what the work must achieve: customer, occasion, price architecture, category need, margin, volume, option count and what "new" means in this context.
Judge against the brief & hold the line: Assess every concept presented against the brief and say so clearly, in the room, with reasons. Your judgement is on brief compliance, newness, customer relevance and commerciality.
Delivery to the brief: As concepts evolve, ensure alignment to the brief, or validate deviation from the brief is for a strategic region. Own this clarity and decision making. Ensure there is strong tension between the brand, regional and commercial needs vs creative innovation and distinctiveness, and this is aligned and resolved appropriately.

Creative Strategy & Planning

Creative plan & direction: own the seasonal creative plan sequenced against go-to-market milestones; facilitate agreement on seasonal direction between the CPO and Co-Founder & Artistic Director, converting it into actionable briefs.
Design language: Hold the team to the Monica Vinader design language across proportion, finish, construction, layering and wearability, using the Co-Founder & Artistic Director and Senior Designer as the reference point, so every piece is recognisably MV. You will apply and defend a standard you did not personally set
Commercial brief: Respond to the annual Product Brief and seasonal commercial briefs with viable design options against price architecture, category need, margin and volume expectations
Trends & aesthetic benchmarking: Ensure trend, material and competitor benchmarking happens to a defined cadence, is properly briefed into the team, and converts into design opportunities that land in the seasonal plan
Originality & IP: Own originality assessment at concept stage, and the IP and design registration gates

Briefing, Critique & Design Process

Design exploration: Ensure multiple routes are explored against every brief and properly finessed before a supplier is briefed
Critique & sign off: Own the design calendar and chair critique. Give a clear view, drive to a decision rather than another round, record it. You sign off that the brief is met and the work can enter development
Supplier briefing & cost: Own that supplier briefs are complete and on time, with technical content authored by the Head of Product Development. Hold the team to cost targets at concept stage, and champion component reuse to cut cost, lead time and complexity

Development Milestones & Critical Path (Accountable)

Critical path & sample approval: hold accountability for development milestones against the critical path (delivery led by the Head of Product Development)
Viability, quality & escalation: ensure designs are viable, manufacturable and meet quality standards; use returns/repairs insight to design out known failure modes; surface slippage, cost or quality risk to the CPO early, with options to solve.
Process ownership: own and continuously improve the NPD process end to end, including gate definitions and the calendar of alignment moments between Design, Merchandising, Supply and Brand.

Design & Development Team Leadership

Lead the team: lead, coach and develop three direct reports (product development, senior design, junior design), setting clear objectives and giving direct feedback. Lead creative specialists without being their creative author — your authority comes from clarity, judgement and advocacy, not out-designing them.
Learn the craft: get fluent in MV's materials, constructions and manufacturing constraints quickly, so you can support the team in the detail, not just manage it.
Resourcing & founder mentorship: structure workload against the product plan, flagging resourcing risk early; support the founder-led mentorship the Co-Founder & Artistic Director gives the design team.
Fixed-term handover: document process, decisions and design intent throughout the contract, and develop the team so the function is fully transferable at handover — holding the team steady through the period of transition.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Integration

Brand, Merchandising, Supply: partner with Brand on consistent product storytelling; with Merchandising/Category on assortment architecture and range rationalisation; with Supply & Quality on cost, capacity and sourcing decisions, engaging early so supplier capability shapes the range as it's built.
Sustainability, trade & trading forums: design within MV's responsible sourcing commitments; support trade, wholesale and regional requirements; represent Design & Development in range review and go-to-market forums, defending decisions with commercial reasoning.
Presentation & ambassadorship: own the Seasonal Product Presentation and timely issue of design assets; represent Design & Development to the ELT, the wider business, and independently on supplier visits and sourcing trips; keep the design studio a functional, inspirational creative space.

What You’ll Bring

Category background: A jewellery background is not required — we're open to leaders from adjacent design-led categories (fashion, accessories, footwear, watches, eyewear, leather goods, homeware, beauty, premium consumer product), provided you've driven a design and development pipeline at pace and with rigour, and can build technical fluency quickly.
Point of view: A clear, expressible point of view on customer, commerciality, newness and process one you'll voice in the room, defend under challenge from senior stakeholders including the founder and CPO, and commit to fully once a decision is made.
Calendar ownership: Proven end-to-end ownership of a product calendar (brief → concept → development → sign off → launch), holding a Head of Product Development to account without being the deepest technical expert in the room.
Organisation: Exceptional organisation across complex, multi-workstream calendars with many dependencies — evidence of building or fixing a critical path, not just working to one.
Range of altitude: Comfortable operating strategically and in the detail of a range plan, critical path or technical pack — this is a small, fast team.
Leadership of creative people: A track record of leading designers or other creative specialists and demonstrably improving their output.

Capability Framework Alignment

Applies Knowledge with Impact: Connects design decisions to margin, sell-through and customer relevance; anticipates cost, supply and quality risk at concept stage.
Communicates Effectively: Translates ambiguous or open creative input into clear, actionable briefs.
Coaches & Develops Others: Creates a development culture with direct, specific feedback.
Challenges & Commits: Leads constructive challenge on creative direction, then commits fully and unifies the team.
Embraces Change: Reframes ambiguity as opportunity and pivots priorities without losing momentum.

To be successful at Monica Vinader, it helps if you...

Are hands-on, solutions-focused, and entrepreneurial
Collaborate openly with humility, honesty, and humour
Embrace learning, teaching, and personal growth
Stay resilient, adaptable, and self-motivated in a creative environment
Speak up when you don’t know—and act fast to figure it out

Additional Requirements

Ability to document your authorisation to work in the United Kingdom.

Travel Requirements

This role requires 2-3 days in our Norfolk office. Outside of this, hybrid working is an option or being based in the London office.

Regular travel oversees (Italy, India, Thailand) 1-2 times per year

Our Aims and Values

Our mission is to be the leading accessible luxury brand, by delivering outstanding quality, design and customer service. We are:

Customer Obsessed

We put our customers at the centre of every decision and deliver thoughtful, personal experiences.

Caring

We act with respect and empathy for people, communities, and the planet.

Fast Paced

We move with focus and flexibility to make progress quickly and decisively.

Exceptional

We hold ourselves to high standards and are always learning, improving, and raising the bar.

Commercial

We make smart, data-led decisions that create long-term value for the business and our customers.

Monica Vinader as a global business makes the following inclusive culture pledge:

Our jewellery is for everyone and so is our community. Together, we will continue to implement sustainable changes to ensure that

The Office of University Development maximizes private support for the University of Michigan.

You will develop short- and long-term strategies to secure major and planned gifts ($100,000 or more) in collaboration with senior academic leaders and development colleagues within a decentralized development environment. Your primary responsibilities will be met through regular visits to U-M constituents within your assigned region. Functional Supervision of Shared Project and Administrative Coordinator

Direct Fundraising (70%)

Manage a portfolio of ~60-80 major gift prospects with emphasis to those prospects who require a university-wide lens (multiple degrees, demonstrated interest in multiple schools or programs).
Provide leadership for the region's major and planned gift activities by focusing on prospects under personal management and supporting solicitations directed by other staff. Ensure that major gift prospects are cultivated and solicited deliberately.
Keep a pace of discovery work throughout the region.
Maintain a pace of 120+ visits, 15+ asks, and 10+ closed gifts per year.

Strategic Leadership and SCCU Collaboration (20%)

Work with our Senior Director of Major Gifts, Midwestern States to plan and lead a regional fundraising strategy that supports prospect/donor identification, engagement, solicitation, and stewardship.
Plan and execute events that directly support regional goals.
Develop collaborative, productive relationships with our SCCU colleagues.
Advise our senior campus leadership (deans, directors, executive officers) on donor strategy and trip planning.
Attend quarterly retreats with our National Major Gifts Team and retreats with the Major Gifts Programs in the Office of University Development.

Recruit and sustain a volunteer network and committee structure in the region to multiply efforts in prospect identification, cultivation, and solicitation.
Provide expanded opportunities for prospects to engage with Michigan's academic leaders and one another.
Be a lead for our Dallas and Houston Campaign Councils during campaign periods.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent education and experience.
Five or more years of development experience in major gifts or other related fields like marketing, banking, or sales experience.
Sound knowledge of laws, practices, and philosophy of charitable giving.
Experience with financial development and/or sales productivity.
Experience working with and/or managing volunteers in some (preferably professional) capacity.

Overview

Baker Tilly is a leading advisory, tax and assurance firm, providing clients with a genuine coast-to-coast and global advantage in major regions of the U.S. and in many of the world’s leading financial centers – New York, London, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago and Boston. Baker Tilly US, LLP is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services to its clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities provide tax and business advisory services to their clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms.

Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP, trading as Baker Tilly, are independent members of Baker Tilly International, a worldwide network of independent accounting and business advisory firms in 141 territories, with 43,000 professionals and a combined worldwide revenue of $5.2 billion. Visit bakertilly.com or join the conversation on LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram.

Please discuss the work location status with your Baker Tilly talent acquisition professional to understand the requirements for an opportunity you are exploring.

Baker Tilly is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable federal, state or local law.

Any unsolicited resumes submitted through our website or to Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, employee e-mail accounts are considered property of Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, and are not subject to payment of agency fees. In order to be an authorized recruitment agency ("search firm") for Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, there must be a formal written agreement in place and the agency must be invited, by Baker Tilly's Talent Attraction team, to submit candidates for review via our applicant tracking system.

Job Description

The Business Development Director at Baker Tilly is a senior-level, strategic role focused on accelerating growth across the firm’s Tax, Assurance, and Consulting practices. This leader is directly responsible for identifying and developing new business opportunities within the Construction, Hospitality & Professional Services (CHPS) sector in an assigned territory, while building, managing, and expanding strong client relationships.

The Director serves as a key member of the CHPS Industry Practice leadership team, partnering with practice leaders to shape and execute go-to-market strategies and drive industry-focused growth initiatives. This includes collaborating across service lines to develop innovative, value-driven solutions that support organizations across construction, infrastructure development, hospitality, restaurants, and professional services firms. This position requires a strong understanding of market dynamics, operational transformation, capital investment cycles, labor and workforce pressures, and regulatory considerations impacting CHPS sectors. It is critical to enhancing Baker Tilly’s market position and delivering differentiated value to clients navigating project-based revenue models, margin pressures, labor constraints, evolving customer expectations, and digital transformation.

jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Buying growth — this role has no paid media, no ad spend, and no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
It’s great to work at a place where people are truly committed to serving our students! We’re committed to bringing passion and energy to our College.

Visit our Life Page on LinkedIn to explore our dynamic campus culture, hear from current employees, and discover what makes Bucks County Community College a great place to work!

Bucks County Community College seeks a highly analytical, entrepreneurial, and operationally focused professional to serve as the Director of Operations for the Division of Workforce & Strategic Partnerships. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Workforce & Strategic Partnerships, this position serves as the division's senior operational leader responsible for improving operational effectiveness and advancing business performance through financial analysis, operational execution, utilization strategies, and performance management in support of priorities established by the Vice President.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the day-to-day operational leadership of the division and directly supervises the Associate Vice President of Workforce Development, the Executive Director of Community Education & Professional Certification, and the Executive Director of Corporate College & Customized Training. Through these leaders, the position ensures consistent execution of divisional priorities, operational accountability, and achievement of financial, enrollment, and performance objectives.

This position strengthens divisional performance through data-informed decision-making, business modeling, operational coordination, and continuous improvement. The Director supports revenue-generating programs through operational execution, financial analysis, and performance optimization while helping ensure the long-term financial sustainability of workforce, public safety, and community education programming.

Essential Functions

Business Performance

Support divisional revenue generating programs through operational execution, business analysis, and implementation of priorities established by divisional leadership.
Conduct market, enrollment, utilization, and operational analyses to identify opportunities to improve program performance, increase efficiency, and expand high-demand offerings.
Support implementation and operational optimization of divisional initiatives, programs, and revenue-generating activities through scheduling, utilization, pricing analysis, and performance monitoring.
Develop business cases, pricing analyses, and financial models to evaluate program feasibility, operational sustainability, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to maximize utilization of divisional facilities, classrooms, labs, and training centers, including evening, weekend, and year-round programming.
Evaluate program performance and recommend operational improvements to strengthen enrollment, resource utilization, earned revenue, and long-term sustainability.

Financial Strategy & Analytics

Lead financial and operational analyses to support divisional decision-making, resource allocation, and performance improvement.
Work with the Executive Director, Business Management to provide program-level financial and operational analyses, including cohort economics, program-level P&L analysis, cost-per-student and cost-per-completer analysis, revenue and margin performance, break-even modeling, enrollment forecasting, and scenario planning.
Develop multi-year financial projections and operational business models to support divisional planning.
Monitor divisional financial performance and provide recommendations to improve efficiency, sustainability, and operational outcomes.
Partner with the Finance Office to support budget development, forecasting, expense monitoring, financial reporting, and divisional planning.
Prepare executive-level reports, dashboards, and analyses for senior leadership, Cabinet discussions, Board reporting, and institutional planning efforts.
Provide financial and operational analysis to support workforce grants, funding proposals, and divisional investments.

Division Operations & Leadership

Provide direct leadership and supervision for the Community Education & Professional Certification, Workforce Development, and Corporate College & Customized Training units through the direct management of the Associate Vice President and Executive Directors responsible for these areas.
Translate the strategic direction established by the Vice President into operational plans and ensure consistent execution, accountability, and achievement of divisional goals.
Develop, streamline, document, and continuously improve operational systems, business processes, and cross-functional workflows to increase efficiency, accountability, responsiveness, and scalability across the division.
Direct operational planning for divisional facilities and training sites, including classroom and laboratory utilization, scheduling optimization, resource allocation, and space management.
Directly supervise the Associate Vice President of Workforce Development, the Executive Director of Community Education & Professional Certification, the Executive Director of Corporate College & Customized Training, and assigned operational and administrative personnel; establish performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, innovation, collaboration, and service excellence.
Monitor operational performance across all functional areas and work with divisional leaders to improve enrollment, revenue, customer service, operational effectiveness, and resource utilization.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, public administration, workforce development, higher education administration, organizational leadership, or a related field.
Five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in operations, business performance, financial analysis, strategic implementation, or organizational leadership.
Demonstrated experience leading senior leaders and managing multi-unit operations.
Demonstrated experience supporting revenue-generating operations, financial modeling, program performance improvement, or business operations.
Strong analytical and financial skills with experience interpreting data to drive operational and business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Exceptional communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate effectively in a dynamic environment.
Proficiency with spreadsheets, dashboards, reporting tools, and enterprise administrative systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in business administration, organizational leadership, workforce development, finance, or a related discipline.
Experience in workforce development, continuing education, public safety training, or complex operational environments.
Experience with program-level financial management, P&L analysis, operational performance improvement, or business operations.
Knowledge of grants management, workforce funding, apprenticeship/pre-apprenticeship programs, and operational planning.
Experience with higher education or workforce technology systems, including Workday, Ellucian Colleague, Campus Marketplace, CRM systems, or workforce reporting tools.
Demonstrated success improving operational performance, supporting program growth, or enhancing earned revenue in a complex organization.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office environment with regular travel between Bucks County Community College campuses and workforce training locations. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support workforce programs, public safety training, operational priorities, and divisional initiatives.

SALARY RANGE
$85,112 - $100,000 (commensurate with experience)

Benefits

Bucks County Community College offers an exceptional benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, prescription plans, 403B pension plan, life insurance, short & long-term disability, generous paid time off, tuition waivers, tuition assistance, wellness center, cafeteria, and free parking on a beautiful Bucks County campus.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employment with the College will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with College's policies.

APPLICATION

Apply online at: https://bucks.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/BCCC

Applications must consist of a letter of application addressing this specific position and the candidate’s interest and qualifications for coming to Bucks County Community College, resume/CV, and professional references. References will not be contacted without prior permission. Finalists may be asked to provide additional materials.

DEADLINE

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

We are proud to be an organization that embraces the value of bringing diverse, talented, and committed people together. The fastest way to breakthrough innovation is when diverse ideas come together in an inclusive environment. We encourage our colleagues to respectfully challenge one another’s thinking and approach problems collectively. We are an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.

Please Note: At this time, the College does not provide work visa sponsorships. To be considered for employment at Bucks County Community College, applicants must be permitted to legally work in the United States without employer sponsorship. Bucks County Community College participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing
jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing, you will lead product marketers to acquire new accounts, shape and implement product-specific marketing strategies, focus on performance metrics, and deliver measurable results. You will accelerate growth through continuous test-and-learn agenda, improvement of paid marketing efforts, and expert allocation of marketing investments. Your team will ideate, plan, launch, measure, and optimize marketing campaigns to drive sustainable growth at efficient Cost Per Account (CPAs). You will be accountable for a large marketing budget, and you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders such as Brand, Product, Risk, and Analytics to drive growth via both new-to-USAA members as well as cross-selling to existing members. Strong analytical skills, business acumen, and entrepreneurial spirit are key to success in this role.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week.
This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX, Plano, TX, Phoenix, AZ, Colorado Springs, CO, Charlotte, NC, or Tampa, FL (Chesapeake, VA – Property and Casualty roles ONLY). Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Responsible for fully digital-first marketing lifecycle, inclusive of strategy, member research, planning, direct response marketing, agency management, creative development, compliant execution, analytics and optimization, and performance management for a subset of products that they support.
Develop and implement marketing plans and campaigns to build and deepen USAA's relationship with existing members, and drive acquisition of new members.
Manage multiple product marketing budgets to deliver sustainable growth at efficient Cost per Account (CPAs) at scale.
Accountable for digital acquisition experience, lead adoption of new ways of working, and leverage storytelling to drive understanding & adoption of change.
Adopt & lead a team to embrace safe & sound business practices at scale.
Provide thought leadership within and keen awareness of the external digital space, with established network of external partners to inspire out-of-box thinking.
Significant knowledge in product related regulations, and risk and compliance requirements.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is never bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, 2 Hour Learning - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Fundraising of any kind is off your plate — no capital campaigns, donor cultivation, or major gifts
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years in a role built on high-stakes relationships: head of school, fundraising, enterprise sales, private wealth management, or client success
Direct, repeated work with ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) families, such as households earning $1M+ a year or families paying full tuition at an elite private school
Experience in a parent-facing or client-facing role at an independent or private K-12 school, or in UHNW client services
At least one example of personally leading a sensitive situation to resolution: a parent crisis, a staff investigation, a press inquiry, or a regulator interaction
A track record of holding a standard when influential people push back on it
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area, and able to work on-site full-time, including evening and weekend events
Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

About 2 Hour Learning

Education is broken, but 2 Hour Learning is proving it doesn’t have to be. They’re tearing down the outdated one-size-fits-all model and replacing it with AI-driven personalized learning that helps kids master academics in just two hours a day.

With students consistently ranking in the top 1-2% nationally and the top 20% achieving an astonishing 6.5x growth, they’re proving that smarter learning is possible. At 2 Hour Learning, it’s talent and performance that matter.

They offer a dynamic, on-campus and remote-friendly environment where innovators, educators, and AI specialists can be a part of fixing a broken school system.

2 Hour Learning is reprogramming learning for the AI era.

jobs.description:
Company Description:
LEAD Training is a Cincinnati-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit that equips young people from kindergarten through young adulthood with life and career readiness skills. The organization designs and delivers programs focused on career readiness, life skills, and social-emotional learning (SEL), with a mission to support students who may feel stymied or unsupported. Through initiatives such as the High School Workforce Initiative, customized employability modules, company partnerships, and career coaching, LEAD helps students develop confidence and plan viable post-secondary paths, whether enrolled, enlisted, or employed.

Role Description:
The Medical & Behavioral Health Program Director is a full-time, on-site role based in Cincinnati, OH. This position oversees the design, implementation, and evaluation of medical and behavioral health components across LEAD’s High School Workforce Initiative programs, ensuring they align with best practices in mental and behavioral health and support students’ career pathway development. The Director will manage day-to-day program operations, including coordinating services, behavioral health credential instruction at local high schools , providing individualized post-graduation career guidance for students, supervising students on internships, implementing K-8 career and life-skill programming, organizing medical and behavioral health events, coordinating CNA and phlebotomy training across multiple schools (instructing if certified), and monitoring case management activities to support student success. Responsibilities include collaborating with school partners and community organizations, developing and refining program curricula, tracking outcomes and reporting on program impact, and ensuring compliance with relevant standards and guidelines. The role also involves contributing to grant reports as needed, supporting staff engagement in the program, and promoting a safe, inclusive environment for all students.

Qualifications

Strong foundation in Mental Health, Behavioral Health, Nursing, or Healthcare, or Psychology, with the ability to apply evidence-informed practices in youth-focused programming.
Experience with Case Management, including assessment, service coordination, and follow-up to support student well-being and progress.
Demonstrated ability in Program Development, such as designing, implementing, and evaluating medical and behavioral health programs or services.
Relevant education in psychology, social work, nursing, social work, counseling, public health, or a related field; advanced degree or licensure (e.g., LISW, LPCC, LCSW, LMHC) is preferred.
Experience working with youth or school-based populations, especially in diverse or underserved communities.
Strong communication, collaboration, and leadership skills, with the ability to work effectively with educators, community partners, and multidisciplinary teams.
Ability to analyze data, document outcomes, and use findings to improve program quality and impact.
Commitment to equity, trauma-informed care, and culturally responsive practices.

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

You will accelerate growth through continuous test-and-learn agenda, improvement of paid marketing efforts, and expert allocation of marketing investments. Your team will ideate, plan, launch, measure, and optimize marketing campaigns to drive sustainable growth at efficient Cost Per Account (CPAs). You will be accountable for a large marketing budget, and you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders such as Brand, Product, Risk, and Analytics to drive growth via both new-to-USAA members as well as cross-selling to existing members. Strong analytical skills, business acumen, and entrepreneurial spirit are key to success in this role.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week.
This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX, Plano, TX, Phoenix, AZ, Colorado Springs, CO, Charlotte, NC, or Tampa, FL (Chesapeake, VA – Property and Casualty roles ONLY). Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Responsible for fully digital-first marketing lifecycle, inclusive of strategy, member research, planning, direct response marketing, agency management, creative development, compliant execution, analytics and optimization, and performance management for a subset of products that they support.
Develop and implement marketing plans and campaigns to build and deepen USAA's relationship with existing members, and drive acquisition of new members.
Manage multiple product marketing budgets to deliver sustainable growth at efficient Cost per Account (CPAs) at scale.
Accountable for digital acquisition experience, lead adoption of new ways of working, and leverage storytelling to drive understanding & adoption of change.
Adopt & lead a team to embrace safe & sound business practices at scale.
Provide thought leadership within and keen awareness of the external digital space, with established network of external partners to inspire out-of-box thinking.
Significant knowledge in product related regulations, and risk and compliance requirements.
Thrive working with cross-functional teams. Effective change agent that can get the job done and push mission forward while managing multiple stakeholder interests and expectations along the way.
Keep USAA brand and our mission to serve the military community at the forefront of new marketing practice.
Attract, develop, expand, and retain high performing teams of marketing professionals that deliver outcomes and key results.
Cultivate talent through coaching and training.
Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

Education

Bachelor's degree; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience. MBA preferred.

10+ years of relevant work experience in financial services with hands-on marketing experience in conversion channels (i.e. Paid Search, Affiliates, Direct Mail).
4+ years of people leadership experience in building, managing and/or developing high-performing teams required.
Experience collaborating with key resources and stakeholders, influencing decisions, and managing work to achieve strategic goals required.
Executive-level business acumen in the areas of business operations, industry practices and emerging trends required.
Demonstrated ability to create and articulate a vision for product marketing organization.
Ability to seek and analyze data from variety of resources to support marketing decisions and alignment with key stakeholders.
Demonstrated proficiency in Product Marketing, including setting growth objectives, developing marketing plans, performance reporting, and driving incremental growth consumer definition, situation assessment, financial analysis, and marketing strategy.
Demonstrated proficiency in marketing data analytics.
Excellent communication skills (verbal and written) with the ability to adjust communication style based on the audiences.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze and evaluate information.
Ability to exercise appropriate judgment by using information and knowledge to make timely, effective decisions.
Ability to adjust scope or resources as appropriate, mitigating potential risk to projects.

What Sets You Apart

5+ years of Property & Casualty product marketing experience, with a focus on auto insurance acquisition. Proven success driving growth in a direct-to-consumer model across offline and digital channels, including Paid Search, Affiliates, and Direct Mail.
Demonstrated expertise in direct-to-consumer product marketing, including growth planning, marketing strategy, performance measurement, financial analysis, and data-driven decision making.
Demonstrated expertise in audience strategy and lifecycle marketing, including audience definition, segmentation, personalization, and engagement strategies that drive customer acquisition, deepening, retention, and lifetime value.
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and modern marketing automation, personalization, and customer data platforms.
Deep understanding of the P&C insurance business and financial drivers, with the ability to connect marketing investments and strategies to portfolio performance, profitability, growth objectives, and P&L outcomes.
Exceptional communication, influence, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build alignment across a complex matrixed organization and effectively engage senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Proven ability to build strong marketing partnerships, align audience strategies, optimize customer journeys, and deliver integrated programs that drive measurable business outcomes.
Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex data and market insights into actionable recommendations and executive-level decisions, particularly within the P&C market.
Experience working in and/or leading cross-functional agile teams, serving as a team lead or product owner, and setting priorities and strategic direction.
US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner.

And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is never bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing
jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing, you will lead product marketers to acquire new accounts, shape and implement product-specific marketing strategies, focus on performance metrics, and deliver measurable results. You will accelerate growth through continuous test-and-learn agenda, improvement of paid marketing efforts, and expert allocation of marketing investments. Your team will ideate, plan, launch, measure, and optimize marketing campaigns to drive sustainable growth at efficient Cost Per Account (CPAs). You will be accountable for a large marketing budget, and you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders such as Brand, Product, Risk, and Analytics to drive growth via both new-to-USAA members as well as cross-selling to existing members. Strong analytical skills, business acumen, and entrepreneurial spirit are key to success in this role.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week.
This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX, Plano, TX, Phoenix, AZ, Colorado Springs, CO, Charlotte, NC, or Tampa, FL (Chesapeake, VA – Property and Casualty roles ONLY). Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Responsible for fully digital-first marketing lifecycle, inclusive of strategy, member research, planning, direct response marketing, agency management, creative development, compliant execution, analytics and optimization, and performance management for a subset of products that they support.
Develop and implement marketing plans and campaigns to build and deepen USAA's relationship with existing members, and drive acquisition of new members.
Manage multiple product marketing budgets to deliver sustainable growth at efficient Cost per Account (CPAs) at scale.
Accountable for digital acquisition experience, lead adoption of new ways of working, and leverage storytelling to drive understanding & adoption of change.
Adopt & lead a team to embrace safe & sound business practices at scale.
Provide thought leadership within and keen awareness of the external digital space, with established network of external partners to inspire out-of-box thinking.
Significant knowledge in product related regulations, and risk and compliance requirements.
Thrive working with cross-functional teams. Effective change agent that can get the job done and push mission forward while managing multiple stakeholder interests and expectations along the way.
Keep USAA brand and our mission to serve the military community at the forefront of new marketing practice.
Attract, develop, expand, and retain high performing teams of marketing professionals that deliver outcomes and key results.
Cultivate talent through coaching and training.
Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

Education

Bachelor's degree; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience. MBA preferred.

What You Have

10+ years of relevant work experience in financial services with hands-on marketing experience in conversion channels (i.e. Paid Search, Affiliates, Direct Mail).
4+ years of people leadership experience in building, managing and/or developing high-performing teams required.
Experience collaborating with key resources and stakeholders, influencing decisions, and managing work to achieve strategic goals required.
Executive-level business acumen in the areas of business operations, industry practices and emerging trends required.
Demonstrated ability to create and articulate a vision for product marketing organization.
Ability to seek and analyze data from variety of resources to support marketing decisions and alignment with key stakeholders.
Demonstrated proficiency in Product Marketing, including setting growth objectives, developing marketing plans, performance reporting, and driving incremental growth consumer definition, situation assessment, financial analysis, and marketing strategy.
Demonstrated proficiency in marketing data analytics.
Excellent communication skills (verbal and written) with the ability to adjust communication style based on the audiences.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze and evaluate information.
Ability to exercise appropriate judgment by using information and knowledge to make timely, effective decisions.
Ability to adjust scope or resources as appropriate, mitigating potential risk to projects.

What Sets You Apart

5+ years of Property & Casualty product marketing experience, with a focus on auto insurance acquisition. Proven success driving growth in a direct-to-consumer model across offline and digital channels, including Paid Search, Affiliates, and Direct Mail.
Demonstrated expertise in direct-to-consumer product marketing, including growth planning, marketing strategy, performance measurement, financial analysis, and data-driven decision making.
Demonstrated expertise in audience strategy and lifecycle marketing, including audience definition, segmentation, personalization, and engagement strategies that drive customer acquisition, deepening, retention, and lifetime value.
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and modern marketing automation, personalization, and customer data platforms.
Deep understanding of the P&C insurance business and financial drivers, with the ability to connect marketing investments and strategies to portfolio performance, profitability, growth objectives, and P&L outcomes.
Exceptional communication, influence, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build alignment across a complex matrixed organization and effectively engage senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Proven ability to build strong marketing partnerships, align audience strategies, optimize customer journeys, and deliver integrated programs that drive measurable business outcomes.
Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex data and market insights into actionable recommendations and executive-level decisions, particularly within the P&C market.
Experience working in and/or leading cross-functional agile teams, serving as a team lead or product owner, and setting priorities and strategic direction.
US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner.

Compensation range: The salary range for this position is: $169,880.00 - $305,780.00

USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).

Compensation:
USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position.

Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.

The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.

Long Term Incentive Plan: Cash payment for Executive level roles only, representing a cash payment which is both time and performance based.

Benefits:
At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.

For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com.

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis, this posting will remain open until the position is filled. Thus, interested candidates are encouraged to apply the same day they view this posting.

USAA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
