new_jobs.title: Ambulatory Care Chief Operating Officer (COO)
new_jobs.description:
Description

For more information about this position, check out the brochure here.

WHAT WE OFFER:
The County of Ventura offers an attractive compensation and benefits package. The salary range for this position is $177,096.97 - $247,935.76
annually, depending on qualifications. An employee in this position will also be eligible for the following:

General Salary Increase: A general salary increase of 3.5%, effective December 20, 2026, and 3.5% effective December 19, 2027.
Educational Incentive: Additional cash payment of 2.5% for completing an associate degree, 3.5% for a bachelor's degree, or 5% for a graduate degree each pay period.
Executive Annual Leave: The selected candidate will earn 248 hours per year, increasing to 288 hours after 5 years of service, 328 hours after 10 years of service, and 368 hours after 15 years of service. Credit for prior public service may be considered (Management Resolution,
1202A).
Annual Leave Redemption: The ability to “cash in” or redeem up to 100 hours of Annual Leave per year after using 80 hours of annual leave within the previous 12 months (Management Resolution,
1207).
Holidays: 13 paid days annually, including a scheduled floating holiday.
Deferred Compensation: Eligible to participate in the County's 401(k) Shared Savings Plan and/or the Section 457 Plan. This position is eligible for up to a 3% match on your 401(k)contributions. Effective February 9, 2024 (and annually thereafter), eligible employees meeting the criteria in Sec. 1907 of the Management Resolution will receive a two percent (2%) of their annualized compensation non-elective contribution into their 401(k) account.
Health Insurance Plans: Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents. A flexible credit allowance of up to $1,024.11 biweekly, depending on enrollment plan tier.
Flexible Spending Accounts: Boost your spending power by reimbursing yourself with pre-tax dollars for IRS-approved dependent care and health care expenses.
Pension Plan: Both you and the County contribute to the County’s Retirement Plan. If eligible, you may establish reciprocity with other public retirement systems, such as CalPERS.
Additional Benefits: Incumbents are entitled to County-paid membership in professional organizations related to their position; other benefits include Disability Plans, Employee Assistance Program, Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement, and Wellness Program.
Professional Membership: Eligible for county-paid membership in professional organizations related to the position.

THE POSITION:
Under general direction of and reporting to the Ambulatory Care Chief Executive Officer, the Ambulatory Care Chief Operating Officer is responsible for leading the administrative operations of the Ventura County Ambulatory Care System which comprises 35 clinics, including 19 Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs). The Chief Operating Officer serves as a trusted strategic partner to executive leadership, providing operational expertise, strategic input, and solutions that support organizational priorities and the effective delivery of ambulatory care services.

The ideal candidate will be a seasoned, collaborative executive leader and highly effective communicator who builds strong partnerships and works across teams to break down organizational and system silos. They will bring a system-wide perspective, balancing the needs of individual programs and teams with the broader operational and strategic needs of the organization. The successful candidate will exercise sound judgment, provide meaningful counsel to leadership, and help translate strategic priorities into effective operations. Experience working within a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or similar health care delivery environment is highly desirable.

PAYROLL TITLE:
Ambulatory Care Administrator

AGENCY/DEPARTMENT:
Health Care Agency – Ambulatory Care Administration

This position is at-will and excluded from the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance. Incumbents in this classification are eligible for benefits at the MB2 level.

TENTATIVE SCHEDULE

OPENING DATE: August 25, 2026

CLOSING DATE: Continuous, and applicants are encouraged to apply promptly for immediate consideration. This position may close without notice.

Review of Application Materials: The first review of application materials will occur beginning September 8, 2026. Applications submitted after that will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The County reserves the right to advance exceptionally qualified candidates forward in the process at any time, regardless of the review schedule. To receive prompt consideration, please submit your materials by the first review date. All relevant experience, training and education must be included to determine eligibility.

Examples Of Duties

Duties may include but are not limited to the following:

Directs, coordinates, monitors, and reviews the activities and staff of assigned Ambulatory Care departments to ensure effective and efficient clinical and business operations, including the Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), hospital-licensed clinics, and special programs;
Provides oversight for accreditation review and compliance, safety review, grant development, clinic facilities development, special projects, patient safety, quality assurance, and compliance;
Supervises assigned department managers in the planning, development, and implementation of administrative initiatives, policies, procedures, and objectives;
Evaluates clinical services and implements changes in Ambulatory Care operations, if necessary.
Assists in the development of pro forma financial statements for potential new service lines and/or business lines;
Assists with the development of Ambulatory Care budget, monitors expenditures against the budget, and audits clinical registration and billing data on an ongoing basis;
Participates in negotiations and development of professional service contracts for medical clinics and monitors contract performance. Monitors staff and provider performance against established benchmarks;
Identifies potential problems and generates innovative, creative solutions for Ventura County Ambulatory Care;
Provides periodic reports on status of Ambulatory Care operations and projects for the Executive Director of the Community Health Center board;
May represent Ambulatory Care clinics at meetings and conferences with County and other officials; prepares correspondence and reports as required; and
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Typical Qualifications

EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:

Required

To qualify for this classification, an individual must possess the education and experience that would likely produce the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. An example of qualifying education and experience is:

A bachelor’s degree in health, business, finance or accounting plus four (4) years of responsible administrative experience in a clinic or health care setting, which includes two (2) years of professional experience in a clinic setting.

Substitution: Up to four (4) years of related experience may be substituted for the Bachelor's Degree.

Necessary Special Requirements

Two (2) years of previous professional staff supervisory experience in a clinic setting.
Excellent written communication skills and collaborative abilities must be demonstrated in the completion of the employment application.

HIGHLY DESIRED:

Previous professional experience working with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs).
Previous professional experience supervising managers and organizational leads.
Five (5) or more years of progressively responsible experience related to a clinic system.
Four (4) or more years in an executive or operational leadership role.
Master's degree in a health care related discipline, business, or public administration.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge Of The Following

Principles of clinical systems and healthcare administration;
Data-driven process improvement;
Principles of business and public administration, including budgeting;
Principles and techniques of effective supervision and staff utilization;
Program management including planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting as required by laws, codes and regulations;
Modern ambulatory care organization, practices, supplies, and equipment;
Joint Commission and federal and state regulatory standards regarding healthcare practices in an ambulatory care system;
Methods and techniques of conflict resolution and negotiation;
County, state, and federal legislation applicable to contemporary clinic operations and patient care issues, methods, regulations, and procedures for research;
Methods and techniques of process improvement such as Lean Six Sigma; and
Federally Qualified Health Center compliance standards.

Skilled In The Following

Redesigning systems to improve quality, performance and efficiency; and
Performance measurement and program evaluation.

Ability To Do The Following

Plan, organize, coordinate, develop, and direct the quality and performance improvement program for a clinic network;
Establish and maintain effective relations with managers and staff, and others contacted in the course of work;
Communicate effectively both verbally and in writing;
Evaluate the quality and effectiveness of the healthcare programs and improve areas requiring attention;
Analyze organization, administrative and personnel problems, and recommend sound solutions;
Comprehend, interpret and apply laws, rules, regulations, and procedures affecting medical or healthcare services; and
Lead, motivate, and supervise staff.

Recruitment Process

Responsibilities

To APPLY
for this exceptional career opportunity, please submit your resume and cover letter highlighting your education and increasingly responsible professional experience, including:

Administrative and operational leadership experience within a clinical or clinic system, including Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs);
Supervisory experience, including oversight of managers and organizational leads; and
Executive leadership experience.

Please submit your application in one of the following ways:

Submit an on-line application and attachments (resume and cover letter) at hr.venturacounty.gov.
E-mail your resume and cover letter to: erin.niemi@venturacounty.gov.

RESUME EVALUATION:
All resumes and cover letters will be reviewed weekly beginning September 8, 2026
to determine if the stated requirements are met. All relevant work experience, training and education need to be included in order to determine eligibility.

INTERVIEW PROCESS:
Following a structured evaluation of the resumes, and cover letters, the most qualified candidates will be invited to a panel interview. The interviews may be consolidated into one process or expanded into multiple interviews contingent upon the size and quality of the candidate pool.

BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION :
A thorough pre-employment, post offer background investigation which may include inquiry into past employment, education, criminal background information and driving record may be required for this position. In addition, the successful candidate may be subjected to Live Scan fingerprinting.

For further information about this recruitment, please contact Erin Niemi by e-mail at erin.niemi@venturacounty.gov or by telephone at (805) 654-2568.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

The County of Ventura is an equal opportunity employer to all, regardless of age, ancestry, color, disability (mental and physical), exercising the right to family care and medical leave, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, military or veteran status, national origin, political affiliation, race, religious creed, sex (includes pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), and sexual orientation.

new_jobs.title: Permitting Policy Director
new_jobs.description:
tl;dr
Co-lead Permit Power’s policy development to simplify and streamline permitting, inspection, HOAs, building codes, and product standards to dramatically lower the cost and accelerate the adoption of residential rooftop solar, plug-in solar, and home batteries.
What we do at Permit Power 

Permit Power is an energy affordability non-profit on a mission to make it cheap and easy for American families to power their lives by cutting the red tape that makes home solar and batteries so expensive. 
We are a small but ambitious team that advances common-sense policy fixes in states around the country to modernize processes like permitting and utility interconnection to allow tens of millions more American families to produce their own affordable electricity. 
What you’ll be doing: 

We are looking for a Permitting Policy Director to co-lead our agenda to remove bureaucratic barriers for residential rooftop solar, plug-in solar, and home batteries including streamlining permitting, inspection, homeowner association approvals, and codes and standards. In partnership with Permit Power’s advocacy staff, you’ll serve as a core part of our team to drive legislative change, lead and participate in coalition efforts, and be an internal expert and external thought leader on permit streamlining. A significant portion of your work will likely focus on policies derived from the values of property rights, small government, and consumer choice in conservative and purple states. The specific policies and states will be divided with Permit Power’s current Permitting Policy Director based on existing expertise, geography, and other factors. You will report to the Chief of Policy.
Develop Permit Power's permitting policy agenda:
Formulate and execute a comprehensive policy plan to simplify and streamline permitting and inspection processes for home solar and batteries, with a focus on states with the largest home solar and battery potential, as well as simplifying and streamlining building codes and product safety standards for home solar products such as plug-in solar.  

Oversee the bill-to-law cycle:
Conduct preliminary research for, draft, and vet permitting bill language. Produce advocacy materials, such as talking points, fact sheets, graphics, and reports. In coordination with Permit Power’s advocacy team and outside lobbyists, lobby legislators, their staff, and executive branch officials. Negotiate with opposition. 

Build and drive coalitions:
Develop and manage relationships with partners such as home builders, the solar industry, think tanks, and others to broaden support for a permitting reform agenda and to collaboratively refine and update our state policy priorities.  

Serve as the subject matter expert:
Act as the organization's authority on permitting rules, regulations, and cutting-edge policies like third party permitting and inspection, HOA overreach, and simplified building codes and product standards.

Evaluate compliance and implementation:
Investigate whether jurisdictions are following the bills we pass, whether installers are actively taking advantage of them, and why. Then analyze where implementation is hitting friction points and refine solutions to remove further and persistent barriers to affordable home solar and batteries.

Manage external research and consultants:
Scope external policy research and identify, onboard, and direct consultants to secure high-quality products supporting our permitting policy agenda.

What we’re looking for:  

7+ years of experience in policy development, legislative advocacy, and/or regulatory affairs related to solar, construction, permitting, or government efficiency.

Track record of successfully developing and executing policy agendas that lead to tangible outcomes, particularly within the state legislative arenas.

Sufficient technical expertise with relevant engineering concepts (e.g., electrical, structural, and/or fire safety) to shape our policy approach to permitting and inspection policies, building codes, and product safety standards.

Experience testifying before, interfacing with, and developing materials for policymakers.

Demonstrated ability to build coalitions and partner with stakeholders to achieve policy goals.

Ability to translate complex technical and engineering concepts into clear, accessible language and materials for policymakers, advocates, and the public.

Relationships with energy policy organizations, the building industry, technical consultants, research firms, and think tanks.

What will make you a good fit: 

Entrepreneurial and self-directed.
We are a small team, and you will need to be able to figure out what your goals are and how to achieve them within the set timeframe. 

Outcomes-oriented.
We measure ourselves by how much we can drive down the cost and timelines for installing solar and batteries, and how much more solar and batteries are installed as a result of our work. We are looking for someone who will find fulfillment in achieving those concrete goals. 

Collaborative and low-ego
. We’re a start-up organization and will make many mistakes. We will only succeed if we work together, acknowledge our mistakes, and learn from them. 

Flexible and open-minded.

Comfortable collaborating and finding common ground with stakeholders across the ideological spectrum

Organized and detail-oriented.
No one will be looking over your shoulder, and you will need to take true ownership over the quality of your work and stay on top of your own administrative work. 

Occasional travel:
Willing to travel for team meetings and periodic partner meetings, hearings, and conferences several times a year. 

The salary & benefits you can expect: 

The salary range for this position is $135,000-160,000. This is a full-time, exempt position. Permit Power offers a generous and comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, dental insurance, vision care, pre-tax commuter benefits, FSA, 401k with 5% contribution matching (limits apply). 

Permit Power offers 6 months of paid maternity or paternity leave to bond with a newborn or adopted child within the first year of birth or adoption. 

We are a fully remote team open to candidates anywhere in the U.S.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success, and that is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, respect and sensitivity.
What the Lawyers told us to say

The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so assigned, and are subject to change.
Applications will close September 25, 2026.

new_jobs.description:
Summary

As AI advances, the power of in-person connection is becoming more valuable. Bizly is a market leading platform for booking in-person events and gatherings at venues worldwide. We are the exclusive booking platform for more than a dozen Fortune 500 companies and have recently signed distribution partnerships with the world’s largest travel companies that take our platform to scale. We are hiring a revenue-focused CEO to help us achieve our growth targets.

Description

As the incoming CEO of Bizly, you own the Profit & Lost, set the operating cadence, and align every system, process, and initiative to the company’s revenue goal. You will build direct relationships with enterprise customers, strategic partners, and the board in order to achieve the required alignment towards your plan.
You will inherit a strong and loyal existing enterprise customer base, a robust venue supply network, and signed partnerships that take the company to scale. You are also inheriting two groundbreaking new AI products. You will design and execute the plan to achieve the targets.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who is relatively early in their career and who has high confidence and conviction in their ability to lead and win based on a track record of success and maturity. We’re looking for revenue growth as the primary focus of the role so we’re seeking someone with adept skills and understanding around enterprise sales, and willing to be an IC across a variety of roles as you work to fill priority hires. The right person is resourceful and can do a lot with a small budget by using AI and growth hacking their way. Our next CEO is an execution focused operator, frugal, curious, ethical, and knows how to break tension with humor.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience as a CEO, CRO, COO, founder or other relevant role
Prior direct ownership of a P&L and held company accountability
Enterprise software and/or marketplace experience
Product savvy and AI pilled

Preferred Qualifications

Track record of taking a company to scale
Experience presenting to and managing a board and investors
Hospitality, marketplace, and/or events experience

new_jobs.title: Director of Development, Technology Sector
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Development for Technology Sector at San Jose State University is a frontline fundraiser within University Advancement. The Director develops relationships with technology executives, founders, investors, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders whose interests may span multiple areas of the university. The Director is responsible for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding alumni, parents, friends, and other prospective donors with professional or philanthropic interests in technology, information systems, entrepreneurship, innovation, and related fields. This position operates within a university-wide advancement model and is not assigned exclusively to a particular college, school, or academic unit.

Working collaboratively with advancement colleagues, university leadership, faculty, and program partners, the Director connects donors’ interests with institutional priorities and develops philanthropic opportunities that advance the university’s mission. The Director will manage a portfolio of major-gift prospects and donors, with an emphasis on securing significant commitments in support of university-wide priorities, interdisciplinary initiatives, student success, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technology-enabled education, and other strategic opportunities. The Director of Development reports to the Associate Vice President for Development/Executive Director of the Campaign and works closely with central development, planned giving, corporate and foundation relations, alumni engagement, research and prospect management, donor relations, and campaign operations.

Key Responsibilities

Manage a portfolio of approximately [100–150] prospective donors, with primary responsibility for prospects capable of making major gifts of $50,000 or more
Develop and execute individualized strategies for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of assigned prospects
Conduct a significant number of substantive donor and prospective donor visits and interactions annually, in person and virtually, in accordance with established performance expectations
Prepare and present compelling philanthropic proposals aligned with donors’ interests and the university’s strategic priorities
Solicit outright, multi-year, planned, blended, and other complex gifts in partnership with appropriate advancement colleagues
Maintain a consistent pipeline of prospective donors at various stages of engagement and achieve annual fundraising, solicitation, qualification, and activity goals
Build and maintain relationships with alumni and friends of the university who are founders, entrepreneurs, technology executives, information systems professionals, venture capital and private equity leaders, investors, innovators, and industry partners
Develop a broad understanding of trends and philanthropic interests within technology, information systems, innovation, and entrepreneurial communities
Create engagement strategies that connect technology-oriented constituents to the university through leadership briefings, faculty interactions, student programs, industry discussions and other meaningful experiences
Identify emerging prospective donors within entrepreneurial and technology networks, including individuals whose university affiliation or philanthropic capacity may not yet be fully developed
Help expand the university’s visibility and relationships within key technology and entrepreneurial markets
Represent the full breadth of the university and develop philanthropic opportunities that may cross colleges, schools, departments, centers, institutes, and administrative units
Assist in developing a university-wide philanthropic strategy for engaging technology and information systems entrepreneurs and industry leaders
Ensure that donors receive timely, meaningful, and personalized stewardship
Document prospect contacts, strategies, proposals, and other relevant information accurately and promptly in the advancement database

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Ability to communicate with constituents in a professional and respectful manner
Working knowledge of, or the ability to develop proficiency in, the appropriate and ethical use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), in higher education and administrative contexts
Ability to apply emerging technologies to support operational effectiveness, data-informed decision-making, and service delivery to students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated ability to support continuous improvement and organizational learning through the responsible application of technology within assigned areas of responsibility
Ability to evaluate potential applications, promote responsible, ethical, and equitable use, and ensure alignment with institutional policies, regulatory requirements, and strategic priorities
Ability to identify donors and close gifts of six and seven figures
Ability to navigate the institution/assigned unit and make the appropriate match for donor interests
Ability to engage and support volunteer leadership with their efforts in fundraising, consultation, and advocacy
Skilled in networking and opening doors as well as developing donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategies
Excellent oral and written communication skills
High level of initiative, attention to detail and organization skills
Skilled in successfully managing multiple projects on tight deadlines and under pressure in a dynamic and open environment
Ability to define problems, gather data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions
Proficient in Google Suite and Microsoft Office Suite and ability to utilize fundraising database programs, and learn new tech platforms for project management
Knowledge of clear, audience-appropriate communication practices for students, faculty, and staff, while maintaining a student-centered approach

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in development, major-gift fundraising, constituent engagement, business development, external relations, or a related field.
Experience in building relationships with high-net-worth individuals and securing significant philanthropic or business commitments
Excellent written communication skills
Experience working with complex organizations and translating institutional priorities into compelling philanthropic opportunities
Proficiency with CRM systems

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced Degree
Experience in higher education advancement or business development in private tech related fields
Experience cultivating and soliciting gifts of $100,000 or more
Experience with technology, information systems, venture capital, startup, or entrepreneurial sectors
Experience working with founders, executives, investors, or other high-capacity professional constituencies
Experience developing interdisciplinary or institution-wide philanthropic opportunities
Experience with planned giving, principal gifts, corporate engagement, or campaign fundraising

Compensation

Classification: Administrator II

Anticipated Hiring Range: $10,000/month - $10,167/month

CSU Salary Range: $5,053/month - $16,221/month

The final hiring salary will be commensurate with experience.

San José State University offers employees a comprehensive benefits package typically worth 30-35% of your base salary. For more information on programs available, please see the Employee Benefits Summary .

Application Procedure

Click Apply Now to complete the SJSU Online Employment Application and attach the following documents:

Resume
Letter of Interest

All applicants must apply within the specified application period: August 25, 2026 through September 8, 2026
. This position is open until filled; however, applications received after screening has begun will be considered at the discretion of the university.

Contact Information

People and Culture

jobs@sjsu.edu

CSU Vaccination Policy

The CSU strongly recommends that all individuals who access any in-person program or activity (on- or off-campus) operated or controlled by the University follow COVID-19 vaccine recommendations adopted by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) applicable to their age, medical condition, and other relevant indications and comply with other safety measures established by each campus. The system wide policy can be found at https://calstate.policystat.com/policy/9779821/latest/ and questions may be sent to jobs@sjsu.edu .

Additional Information

Satisfactory completion of a background check (including a criminal records check) is required for employment. SJSU will issue a contingent offer of employment to the selected candidate, which may be rescinded if the background check reveals disqualifying information, and/or it is discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the continued employment of a current CSU employee who was offered the position on a contingent basis.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development, Technology Sector
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Development for Technology Sector at San Jose State University is a frontline fundraiser within University Advancement. The Director develops relationships with technology executives, founders, investors, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders whose interests may span multiple areas of the university. The Director is responsible for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding alumni, parents, friends, and other prospective donors with professional or philanthropic interests in technology, information systems, entrepreneurship, innovation, and related fields. This position operates within a university-wide advancement model and is not assigned exclusively to a particular college, school, or academic unit.

Working collaboratively with advancement colleagues, university leadership, faculty, and program partners, the Director connects donors’ interests with institutional priorities and develops philanthropic opportunities that advance the university’s mission. The Director will manage a portfolio of major-gift prospects and donors, with an emphasis on securing significant commitments in support of university-wide priorities, interdisciplinary initiatives, student success, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technology-enabled education, and other strategic opportunities. The Director of Development reports to the Associate Vice President for Development/Executive Director of the Campaign and works closely with central development, planned giving, corporate and foundation relations, alumni engagement, research and prospect management, donor relations, and campaign operations.

Key Responsibilities

Manage a portfolio of approximately [100–150] prospective donors, with primary responsibility for prospects capable of making major gifts of $50,000 or more
Develop and execute individualized strategies for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of assigned prospects
Conduct a significant number of substantive donor and prospective donor visits and interactions annually, in person and virtually, in accordance with established performance expectations
Prepare and present compelling philanthropic proposals aligned with donors’ interests and the university’s strategic priorities
Solicit outright, multi-year, planned, blended, and other complex gifts in partnership with appropriate advancement colleagues
Maintain a consistent pipeline of prospective donors at various stages of engagement and achieve annual fundraising, solicitation, qualification, and activity goals
Build and maintain relationships with alumni and friends of the university who are founders, entrepreneurs, technology executives, information systems professionals, venture capital and private equity leaders, investors, innovators, and industry partners
Develop a broad understanding of trends and philanthropic interests within technology, information systems, innovation, and entrepreneurial communities
Create engagement strategies that connect technology-oriented constituents to the university through leadership briefings, faculty interactions, student programs, industry discussions and other meaningful experiences
Identify emerging prospective donors within entrepreneurial and technology networks, including individuals whose university affiliation or philanthropic capacity may not yet be fully developed
Help expand the university’s visibility and relationships within key technology and entrepreneurial markets
Represent the full breadth of the university and develop philanthropic opportunities that may cross colleges, schools, departments, centers, institutes, and administrative units
Assist in developing a university-wide philanthropic strategy for engaging technology and information systems entrepreneurs and industry leaders
Ensure that donors receive timely, meaningful, and personalized stewardship
Document prospect contacts, strategies, proposals, and other relevant information accurately and promptly in the advancement database

new_jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Buying growth — this role has no paid media, no ad spend, and no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

new_jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, 2 Hour Learning - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Fundraising of any kind is off your plate — no capital campaigns, donor cultivation, or major gifts
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years in a role built on high-stakes relationships: head of school, fundraising, enterprise sales, private wealth management, or client success
Direct, repeated work with ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) families, such as households earning $1M+ a year or families paying full tuition at an elite private school
Experience in a parent-facing or client-facing role at an independent or private K-12 school, or in UHNW client services
At least one example of personally leading a sensitive situation to resolution: a parent crisis, a staff investigation, a press inquiry, or a regulator interaction
A track record of holding a standard when influential people push back on it
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area, and able to work on-site full-time, including evening and weekend events
Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

About 2 Hour Learning

Education is broken, but 2 Hour Learning is proving it doesn’t have to be. They’re tearing down the outdated one-size-fits-all model and replacing it with AI-driven personalized learning that helps kids master academics in just two hours a day.

With students consistently ranking in the top 1-2% nationally and the top 20% achieving an astonishing 6.5x growth, they’re proving that smarter learning is possible. At 2 Hour Learning, it’s talent and performance that matter.

They offer a dynamic, on-campus and remote-friendly environment where innovators, educators, and AI specialists can be a part of fixing a broken school system.

2 Hour Learning is reprogramming learning for the AI era.

Here’s How They’re Fixing It.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest

Fundraising of any kind is off your plate — no capital campaigns, donor cultivation, or major gifts

Direct, repeated work with ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) families, such as households earning $1M+ a year or families paying full tuition at an elite private school
Experience in a parent-facing or client-facing role at an independent or private K-12 school, or in UHNW client services
At least one example of personally leading a sensitive situation to resolution: a parent crisis, a staff investigation, a press inquiry, or a regulator interaction

new_jobs.title: Senior Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

Joshua Nations is seeking a full-time Senior Development Director
to lead the ministry’s donor development strategy, expand financial partnerships, strengthen donor relationships, and help increase the organization’s long-term revenue capacity.

The Development Director will serve as the senior leader responsible for development strategy, major donor cultivation, donor pipeline management, campaigns, church and business partnerships, and coordination of the development team. This role will work closely with the President/CEO, Grant Writer, Director of Impact Reporting, COO, International Director, Creative Team, and Board of Directors to build a disciplined and sustainable development system.

Joshua Nations’ long-term goal is to increase annual revenue from approximately $1.6 million to $3 million
. The Development Director will play a central role in helping achieve this growth through major gifts, donor upgrades, recurring giving, grant support, strategic campaigns, church partnerships, business partnerships, and new donor acquisition.

Compensation

Salary range: $90,000–$120,000 plus benefits
, commensurate with experience, proven fundraising ability, donor network, leadership capacity, and strategic development expertise.
Joshua Nations may also consider performance-based bonuses or compensation growth tied to clear development goals, healthy donor development practices, and measurable revenue growth.
Joshua Nations does not use commission-based fundraising compensation. Any incentive structure will be designed to honor ethical, relationship-based, ministry-centered fundraising.

Purpose of the Role

The Development Director exists to build and lead a comprehensive development strategy that increases Joshua Nations’ financial capacity while strengthening donor trust, mission alignment, and long-term partnership.

This role is not simply administrative. It is a senior-level, frontline development position requiring relational warmth, strategic thinking, disciplined follow-through, confidence in making financial asks, and the ability to represent Joshua Nations with excellence to donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and ministry partners.

The Development Director will help move Joshua Nations from founder/President-centered fundraising toward a scalable development system that supports continued growth and ministry impact.

Growth Pathway

This role is initially structured as a Development Director
position rather than a Chief Development Officer position because Joshua Nations is still building its formal development infrastructure. The Development Director will be expected to lead and execute donor development strategy, cultivate major gifts, strengthen donor relationships, and produce measurable revenue growth.

As fundraising goals are met and the development function expands, this position may grow into a Chief Development Officer
role. Promotion to Chief Development Officer would be considered based on demonstrated fundraising success, achievement of agreed revenue benchmarks, ability to build scalable development systems, leadership capacity, and the need to hire and manage additional development personnel.

If the Development Director successfully helps Joshua Nations reach its revenue goals, Joshua Nations may build a development team under this role. This pathway is intended to give the right candidate room to grow with the organization while ensuring that future title changes and team expansion are tied to proven results, organizational need, and sustainable revenue growth.

Key Revenue Deliverables

The Development Director will be expected to produce measurable fundraising results.

Required Return-on-Investment Goals

Within 12 Months

The Development Director should raise or directly influence at least 2x their annual base salary
in new revenue, increased giving, or committed pledges.
Based on the salary range, this equals approximately:
$180,000
if salary is $90,000
$240,000
if salary is $120,000

This may include new gifts, donor upgrades, recurring giving, project gifts, major gifts, church partnerships, business partnerships, grants, or reactivated donors.

Within 24 Months

The Development Director should raise or directly influence at least 3.0x their annual base salary
in new revenue, increased giving, or committed pledges.
Based on the salary range, this equals approximately:
$270,000
if salary is $90,000
$360,000
if salary is $120,000

These goals should be understood as minimum benchmarks. The broader expectation is that the Development Director will build a development system capable of helping Joshua Nations move toward the long-term goal of $3 million in annual revenue
.

Primary Responsibilities

1. Development Strategy and Leadership

The Development Director will lead the overall development strategy for Joshua Nations.
Responsibilities include:
Creating and implementing a comprehensive annual development plan.
Building a multi-year revenue growth strategy.
Establishing clear goals for major gifts, recurring giving, grants, campaigns, church partnerships, business partnerships, and donor retention.
Leading the development team, including the Grant Writer and Director of Impact Reporting.
Working with the President/CEO to prioritize top donor relationships and strategic funding opportunities.
Helping the organization move from reactive fundraising to proactive donor development.
Creating systems that support long-term donor cultivation, follow-up, stewardship, and growth.
Providing regular development updates to the President/CEO and appropriate board leadership.

2. Major Donor Cultivation

The Development Director will lead major donor strategy and help build a strong donor pipeline.
Responsibilities include:
Identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors.
Managing a portfolio of high-value current and prospective donors.
Creating individualized cultivation plans for key donors.
Working with the President/CEO on top-level donor relationships.
Making direct financial asks.
Developing a pipeline of donors capable of giving $10,000, $25,000, $50,000, $100,000, or more.

3. Donor Pipeline and Portfolio Management

The Development Director will create a disciplined donor development process.
Responsibilities include:
Building and managing a qualified donor pipeline.
Segmenting donors by giving history, capacity, interests, engagement level, and readiness for cultivation.
Establishing donor touchpoint rhythms.
Tracking donor conversations, asks, proposals, pledges, and next steps.
Ensuring timely donor follow-up.
Maintaining donor records in the CRM or donor management system.
Coordinating with Operations on donor data accuracy and gift tracking.
Reporting monthly on donor pipeline movement, asks made, gifts secured, and future opportunities.

4. Campaigns and Strategic Giving Opportunities

The Development Director will help package Joshua Nations’ ministry priorities into clear and compelling giving opportunities.
Potential funding areas may include:
Bible Training Centers
Church multiplication and disciple-making initiatives
Frontier People Group and DMM projects
Women of Valor
RISE / NextGen
Leadership summits
Curriculum translation and development
Field leader training
Unreached and under-reached regions
Sustainability projects
Regional and national expansion initiatives

5. Church, Business, and Strategic Partnerships

The Development Director will help expand Joshua Nations’ partnership base.
Developing relationships with churches, business leaders, foundations, family offices, and ministry-aligned networks.

6. Donor Stewardship and Communication

The Development Director will help ensure that donors are thanked, informed, and meaningfully connected to the mission.

7. Grant and Foundation Strategy

The Development Director will oversee grant and foundation strategy in partnership with the Grant Writer.

8. Reporting and Accountability

The Development Director will provide consistent reporting on development progress.

Key Performance Indicators

The Development Director will be evaluated through both activity-based and results-based metrics.
Revenue Metrics

2x salary return within 12 months.
3.0x salary return within 24 months.
New revenue raised or directly influenced.
Increased giving from current donors.
Major gifts secured.
Recurring giving growth.
Number of upgraded donors.
Number of reactivated donors.
Church and business partnerships developed.
Grant and foundation revenue supported or secured.
Progress toward Joshua Nations’ long-term $3 million annual revenue goal.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Strong personal alignment with the Christian mission, values, and global vision of Joshua Nations.
Proven experience in fundraising, donor development, major gifts, nonprofit development, ministry partnership development, or a closely related field.
Demonstrated ability to raise significant funds through relationship-based development.
Experience cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Comfort making direct financial asks.
Ability to lead a development strategy and manage development personnel.
Strong organizational discipline and follow-through.
Ability to work independently while remaining accountable to leadership.
High integrity, discretion, and respect for donor confidentiality.
Willingness to travel for donor meetings, church presentations, conferences, ministry events, and partner visits as needed.

Experiential Qualifications

Experience securing gifts of $25,000 or more.
Experience cultivating donors capable of $50,000–$100,000+ gifts.
Experience managing a major donor portfolio.
Experience working in Christian ministry, missions, church networks, or nonprofit organizations.
Experience with grant strategy, foundation relations, or campaign development.
Existing relationships with ministry-minded donors, churches, business leaders, or foundations.
Understanding of international missions, discipleship, church planting, leadership development, and donor stewardship.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development - Meritus College
new_jobs.description:
The Organization: Merit America

The American economy is broken. Today, 53 million working adults–nearly half of the U.S. workforce–do not earn a living wage. These talented workers have few options to advance: college is too long and expensive, full-time boot camp programs don't offer enough flexibility, and online courses don't have the structure or support to translate learning into a new career. The result? Talented workers, disproportionately people of color and women, get stuck in low-wage roles with no way to build a better life for themselves and their families.

Merit America is a national nonprofit that creates pathways to family-sustaining careers for Americans stuck in low-wage work. Our fast, flexible solutions are built for working adults: We start by analyzing tens of millions of job postings to identify in-demand, high-paying tech careers and then work with industry-recognized partners to train for these roles with part-time programs that combine flexible online learning with best-in-class coaching. Finally, we support our learners in their job search, helping them connect with a broad constellation of local and national employers such as JPMorgan Chase and Infosys to land higher-earning, family-sustaining jobs. Merit America is on a mission to build a scalable pathway for workers to join the middle class through merit, not money. Since our founding in 2018, we've generated a projected $1 billion in near-term wage gains for our learners.

The Organization: Meritus College

Meritus College is a new kind of not-for-profit online college, built from the ground up to meet the needs of working adults and career-changers who've been overlooked by traditional higher education.

The problem is clear: only 33% of Pell grant recipients complete their degrees at two-year colleges within 6 years. College has become too rigid, too expensive, and too disconnected from both student realities and career outcomes. Merit College is different. Our online, asynchronous programs and "workplace as laboratory" approach allow students to learn and apply new skills directly to their jobs, while receiving personalized support from dedicated coaches every step of the way. We focus on real-world skills and stackable credentials in high-demand fields, ensuring graduates are prepared for today's jobs and tomorrow's opportunities. Founded in 2025 with an inaugural Associate of Applied Science in Technology and Innovation degree, Merit College is building a mainstream pathway to economic mobility—one designed not for the privileged few, but for the talented many who've too often been left behind.

About The Role

Meritus College doesn't have a century of alumni wealth to call on. What it has is a bold, evidence-backed model, a founding team with credibility in both higher ed and philanthropy, and an open field for building a modern fundraising function that looks more like an early-stage nonprofit startup than a traditional university advancement office.

We're looking for a Director of Development to join this founding team and help build that function. This is a hybrid role: part traditional higher-ed philanthropy (institutional funders and individual donors who care about post-secondary access and attainment), part startup-style fundraising (moving fast, building processes as you go, wearing multiple hats, working with founders, and engaging funders in the mission first - not the endowment).

A successful candidate will:

Manage and expand a portfolio of mission-aligned 6- and 7-figure foundation, corporate, and individual funders who care about economic mobility and the future of higher education.
Translate Meritus College's early outcomes data and founding story (which includes Merit America's success to date) into compelling, fundable narratives.
Move comfortably between the discipline of traditional higher-ed philanthropy (stewardship, reporting, gift agreements) and the speed and resourcefulness of an early-stage startup.
Lead the fundraising strategy to launch Meritus College. Beyond direct portfolio management, this work will include shaping and building new fundraising initiatives and ways of working that meet the needs of a new, innovative higher education model.

This role reports to the Managing Director of Development and works closely with Merit America's broader Development Team and Meritus College's academic and operating leadership.

What You'll Be Doing

The primary responsibilities of the Director of Development will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Build and Advance the Pipeline (50%)

Identify, research, and cultivate new funding relationships across foundations, corporate partners, and individual donors who care about higher-ed innovation and economic mobility, bearing in mind that Meritus College does not have an alumni base to draw from.
Lead proposal development with support from Merit America's Development team, adapting fundraising narratives as Meritus College's model, outcomes, and proof points evolve.
Bring an entrepreneurial lens to prospecting: apply the kind of hustle, creativity, and resourcefulness common in early-stage startup fundraising to a philanthropic context.
Track and analyze pipeline health, funder trends, and outcomes to continuously sharpen strategy.

Manage Donor and Prospect Relationships (30%)

Lead a small portfolio of existing warm prospects and new 6- and 7-figure funding relationships, managing the full cycle from first outreach through solicitation, close, and stewardship – with a goal of advancing $10M in deals to proposal stage (or later) in your first year, with support from the broader Development Team.
Write clear, engaging correspondence that connects Meritus College's data and mission to what funders care about.
Represent Meritus College in funder meetings and presentations, including opportunities to bring in founders/academic leadership for key relationships.
Ensure funders are stewarded and renewed thoughtfully to build long-term trust in a startup college reimagining higher education from the inside out.

Build the Function (20%)

Partner with Meritus College's academic, data, and operations teams to gather the proof points and impact data funders will want to see.
In collaboration with Meritus College leadership, build the advancement function - bringing your expertise and perspectives on how a startup-minded fundraising function should look different from a traditional university advancement office.

What Makes a Successful Candidate

We recognize that people from underrepresented backgrounds are often less likely to apply unless they meet every qualification. Don't let that be the reason you miss out — we encourage you to apply if you demonstrate many, not all, of the following:

Must Haves

Experience Building New Programs in Higher Education

Experience as the fundraising lead, or the close partner to the fundraising lead, on something a college or university was building for the first time: a new degree program, school, campus, institute, accredited entity, or a nonprofit incubated inside an institution.
Working knowledge of accreditation, credit portability and transfer, academic model design, and the diligence institutional funders run on a new or newly accredited program.
Track record of raising money or building partnerships, or of supporting the person or team who did. Familiar with what it takes to build a case for support while the proof points are still accumulating.

Note: we're open to candidates who came to this from the academic, program, or operations side and partnered closely with development. Deep involvement in building a new academic offering, alongside the fundraisers making the case for it, counts here.

Entrepreneurial & Startup Mindset

Bias for action: willing to prospect cold, draft the first version of a proposal template, and figure it out rather than wait for a fully formed process, while working quickly and collaboratively with the development team, college team, and executive leadership. You are self-directed and make good calls with incomplete information.
Genuine comfort with ambiguity: this is a new college inside a growing organization, so strategy, goals, and the pitch itself will shift as we learn. A target funder list may need rebuilding after a new data point comes in. We need someone who finds that energizing.
Track record of leveraging resources including AI to speed up and make more efficient tasks like research, drafting, and prospecting so a small team can punch above its weight.

Communication & Storytelling

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate data and mission into a persuasive case for support.
Comfort with pitching a new institution with credibility and honesty about what's proven and what's still being built.
Confidence shaping an ambiguous narrative with prospective funders, including thinking with agility and creativity in conversations.

Mission Alignment

Genuine belief in expanding access to higher education for working adults and non-traditional students, and enthusiasm for a model that looks different from a traditional four-year college.
Alignment with Merit America's values: Think Big, Deliver Results, Win & Lose Together, Learn Constantly, Care Deeply, Enjoy the Ride.

Nice to Have

Direct experience at a startup, scaling nonprofit, or other fast-moving, resource-constrained organization — comfortable operating without established playbooks, and energized by building rather than maintaining.
Existing relationships with foundations or funders focused on postsecondary attainment, workforce development, or economic mobility.
Experience with Salesforce or a comparable CRM.
Comfort using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) to speed up research, drafting, and prospecting.

Other Logistics

This position is full-time: 4-day work week (Fridays are an operating day if there is a holiday closure during the week)
Travel:
Occasional travel required (up to 25% of time)
Location

Salary

Our goal is to have competitive and equitable compensation. We have a market-based compensation approach, which means we benchmark each role from reputable data sources. We compare our benchmarks against similarly sized non-profit organizations with comparable annual budgets and geographical areas. We pay the same rate for the same roles and adjust to comply with statutory mandates.

Position Summary

As Director of Development, you will put your proven sales and relationship management skills to work driving success and achieving revenue goals through positive engagement with staff and community volunteer leaders throughout Northwest Ohio, Cleveland Ohio and Greater East Ohio.

Utilizing your proven networking skills, you will identify and cultivate relationships with key community leaders and C-Suite corporate partners effectively. This position will be responsible for (6) Walk to End Alzheimer’s events and Do What You Love To End Alzheimer’s. As a recognized leader and fundraiser in the peer-to-peer space, you will coach and inspire your team to build successful event growth strategies through community and volunteer engagement.

You join a high performing team of leaders responsible for the implementation of Walk to End Alzheimer’s®, the world’s largest fundraiser for Alzheimer’s care, support and research; Do What You Love to End ALZ, a signature event of the Alzheimer’s Association, and is one of the fastest growing and unique campaigns of its kind; and Relationship Events/Gala initiatives.

Walk to End Alzheimer’s® ranks as the second-largest peer-to-peer fundraising event in the United States and continues to set the pace as one of the fastest-growing walk events in the country. Do What You Love to End ALZ is leading the peer-to-peer fundraising space with innovation and creativity, providing an excellent opportunity to engage new audiences in the fight to end Alzheimer’s among many diverse activity groups, from the golfing and hiking communities to live streamers and bridge players.

In this key leadership role, you will be responsible for successful implementation of Walk to End Alzheimer’s® and Do What You Love to End ALZ to meet or exceed goals through staff training, coaching and mentoring as well as volunteer recruitment and empowerment, team and individual fundraising cultivation, and through the diligent execution of strategies that align with best and proven practices. You will contribute your professional fundraising leadership experience in leading, coaching and mentoring your team of (6) professional development staff.

This position is a perfect fit for a purpose-driven, mission-minded people leader who inspires others to take initiative to achieve positive and measurable results, demonstrates a positive attitude and takes a pro-active approach to responsibility ownership.

This role is right for you if;

You are an enthusiastic and active member of the community, utilizing your engaging networking skills to build sustainable corporate and community partnerships to achieve organizational revenue goals
You are able to drive success and provide positive engagement with staff and volunteers through coaching, recognition, and mutual accountability
You have successfully recruited, managed, and coached fundraising staff and volunteers to effectively implement best and proven practices to achieve fundraising goals with a priority on Peer-to-Peer initiatives
You are known as a uniter and have successfully built a positive, healthy, and inclusive team environment
Your experience in providing inspirational leadership, oversight and implementation of fundraising programs has resulted in meeting or exceeding revenue goals around mass market events/special events, corporate sponsorship and other corporate gifts, pipeline development for major and planned gifts and other areas of development
You have proven success at building sustainable corporate and community relationships that contribute to achieving event revenue goals, greater community participation and heightened brand awareness
You have managed or are capable of managing multiple volunteer-led mass-market events simultaneously that have resulted in revenue growth year over year
You embrace a challenge and have achieved or surpassed designated revenue and participant goals through team and individual fundraising, corporate solicitation, and community partnerships
You have demonstrated success at prospecting, cultivating and stewarding event teams, sponsors and participants
You have excellent communication and organization skills and are comfortable with managing event budgets, training volunteers, working to set timelines and milestones and using data to affect positive outcomes

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree preferred in sales/business or related field.
5-7 years of proven experience recruiting and mobilizing volunteers and community leaders to achieve goals, preferably in a peer-to-peer fundraising environment OR successful experience leading a team to meet sales targets
Experience with mass market events like Walk is required

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Demonstrated management skills, including the ability to set clear goals, organize projects, establish and manage budgets, and establish accountability processes
Ability to supervise and manage Walk to End Alzheimer’s & Do What You Love staff, including onboarding, training and development
A proven track record at building sustainable corporate and community relationships that contribute to achieving organizational and revenue goals
Proven track record of developing and implementing strategies for identifying, recruiting and engaging high-level and C-Suite volunteer leadership,
Enthusiastic willingness to work with diverse communities and build an inclusive environment
Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% within the assigned territory by car. While most such travel is same day, occasional overnight travel or air travel may be required. Must have valid driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle, good driving record and proof of automobile insurance
Ability and willingness to work evenings and weekends as required for the job
Ability to bend, stoop, lift and transport up to 25 lbs of materials
Strong computer skills, proficient with Microsoft Office products and social media; experience with, or ability to rapidly learn, Luminate/Convio software

Who We Are

The Alzheimer’s Association is the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer’s care, support and research. Our mission is to lead the way to end Alzheimer's and all other dementia– by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support.

The Alzheimer’s Association announced a landmark $100 million investment in research for 2023. This unparalleled commitment is illustrative of the momentum we are building in dementia research — our investments today will lead to breakthroughs tomorrow.

At the Alzheimer’s Association, our employees are at the core of all we do. Our network of more than 1,750 employees across the United States makes a difference each and every day for those impacted by Alzheimer’s and those at risk for the disease.

We warmly invite qualified applicants to consider this opportunity to make a life-changing impact on the millions living with Alzheimer’s, their caregivers and those that may develop the disease in the future. Read on to learn more about the role, then visit our website www.alz.org/jobs to explore who we are and why we've been recognized as a Best Place to Work for the last twelve years in a row.

At the Alzheimer's Association®, we believe that diverse perspectives are critical to achieving health equity — meaning that all communities have a fair and just opportunity for early diagnosis and access to risk reduction and quality care. The Association is committed to engaging underrepresented and underserved communities and responding with resources and education to address the disproportionate impact of Alzheimer’s and dementia.

The Alzheimer’s Association commitment remains steadfast in engaging all communities in our full mission.
